_readme: Owner: Set C. One place for every real-world number. The HUD shows these and the physics uses the same gravity. Set "verified": true and fill "source" with the NASA page only after you have checked the number yourself. Checked on 14 Nov 2026 against the NASA planetary fact sheets (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov).

temperature.note: No NASA page found for the clean room temperature. Earth's average is 15 °C (earthfact.html)

gravity.note: Fact sheet: surface gravity 1.62 m/s², 0.165 of Earth (one-sixth)

temperature.note: Fact sheet: diurnal range at the equator 95 K to 390 K. The old draft said −130 °C at night, which was wrong

pressure.note: Fact sheet: surface pressure (night) 3 x 10^-15 bar

gravity.note: Fact sheet: surface gravity (mean) 3.73 m/s². The old draft said 3.71

temperature.note: Fact sheet: average temperature ~214 K (−59 C)

pressure.note: Fact sheet: 6.36 mb at mean radius, 4.0 to 8.7 mb by season. Earth is 1014 mb, so about 0.6%

gravity.note: A game simplification: the probe is in free fall. Not a measured number

temperature.note: COBE measured the cosmic background at 2.725 K

pressure.note: No NASA page with a number found yet

missions._readme: Owner: Set C (task C-8). Every mission claim in PLAN.md section 12 and every (verify) in STORY.md, checked on 14 Nov 2026. Only claims with verified: true may appear in the game. 'note' says what changed or what to be careful with.

lrv_missions.claim: The Lunar Roving Vehicle was used on Apollo 15, 16 and 17, in 1971 and 1972

a17_place_date.claim: Apollo 17 landed in the Taurus–Littrow valley in December 1972

a17_fender.claim: A rear fender broke on the first moonwalk; the crew built a new one from four maps, duct tape and clamps
a17_fender.value: Fender repaired with maps and clamps
a17_fender.note: Photo as17-137-20979 (12 Dec 1972) shows the repair. A hammer knocked part of the fender off during EVA-1. The idea for the repair came from Mission Control

moon_dust_arcs.claim: With no air on the Moon, dust kicked up by the wheels flies in arcs and falls back; it does not hang in clouds
moon_dust_arcs.value: Ballistic dust, over 2 m high from the Apollo 17 rover
moon_dust_arcs.note: NASA rover paper: lifted particles do not remain suspended; each follows a ballistic trajectory

rover_filmed_liftoff.claim: The rover's TV camera, aimed from Mission Control, filmed the Apollo 17 lunar module lift-off
rover_filmed_liftoff.value: Lift-off filmed from the rover, December 1972
rover_filmed_liftoff.note: Ed Fendell at Mission Control aimed the camera remotely. The rover was parked at the VIP site so the world could watch. The exact date (14 Dec) was not on the page; use 'December 1972'

opportunity_landing.claim: Opportunity landed in January 2004 at Meridiani Planum, inside a small crater called Eagle, after bouncing on airbags
opportunity_landing.note: NASA gives 24 Jan 2004 (US time), which is 25 Jan in UTC. Use 'January 2004'

opportunity_spherules.claim: The small round pebbles ('blueberries') are hematite that formed in water
opportunity_spherules.note: Say 'formed in water'. The exact way they formed is still discussed

opportunity_wind_cleaning.claim: Wind cleaned dust off Opportunity's solar panels and gave it more power
opportunity_wind_cleaning.note: Mission page: the wind had cleaned much of the dust off the rover's solar panels. Driving through whirlwinds on purpose is a game idea, not a real event

opportunity_sol_4712.claim: Opportunity was still working on sol 4,712 (26 April 2017), next to Orion crater on the rim of Endeavour crater
opportunity_sol_4712.note: In the pack: PIA21706, PIA21707, PIA21708

orion_crater_name.claim: Orion crater on Mars was named after the Apollo 16 lunar module
orion_crater_name.value: Named after the Apollo 16 lunar module

opportunity_last_contact.claim: Opportunity's last signal was on 10 June 2018, during a planet-wide dust storm

opportunity_end.claim: NASA declared the mission over on 13 February 2019

viking_landing.claim: The Viking 1 lander touched down on 20 July 1976 in Chryse Planitia

viking_planned.claim: The Viking landers were designed to work for about 90 days
viking_planned.note: Some NASA pages say 'a minimum of 90 days'

viking_end.claim: The Viking 1 lander worked until November 1982, more than six years
viking_end.note: So the line 'I gave them six years' is right

ingenuity_arrival.claim: Ingenuity reached Mars on 18 February 2021, attached under the Perseverance rover, in Jezero crater

ingenuity_cameras.claim: Ingenuity has two cameras on its underside

ingenuity_first_flight.claim: First flight on 19 April 2021: it climbed to 3 m, hovered for 30 seconds and landed
ingenuity_first_flight.note: The first powered, controlled flight on another planet

ingenuity_shadow.claim: Ingenuity photographed its own shadow while hovering on its first flight
ingenuity_shadow.value: Shadow photo from the first flight

ingenuity_planned.claim: Ingenuity was planned for up to 5 test flights over 30 days

ingenuity_total.claim: Ingenuity made 72 flights in almost three years; the last was on 18 January 2024

ingenuity_last_flight.claim: On flight 72 the ground was steep, featureless sand ripples; the navigation system lost track, the landing was hard and the rotor blades broke
ingenuity_last_flight.value: Featureless sand ripples · all four blades broke
ingenuity_last_flight.note: STORY.md says 'smooth sand' and 'a blade tip snaps'. NASA says 'featureless sand ripples', and all four blades broke about a third of the way from the tip

ingenuity_battery.claim: Flights were short: the solar panel charged the batteries for about one 90-second flight per Martian day
ingenuity_battery.note: Later flights lasted up to about 2–3 minutes

mars_thin_air.claim: The air on Mars is less than 1% as thick as Earth's
mars_thin_air.note: 6.36 mbar against Earth's 1014 mbar. Say 'less than 1%', not 'about 1%'

pioneer_builder.claim: Pioneer 10 was built by TRW and delivered to Cape Kennedy in February 1972

pioneer_plaque.claim: Pioneer 10 carries a plaque that shows where and when it came from

pioneer_launch.claim: Pioneer 10 launched on 2 March 1972, the same year as Apollo 17
pioneer_launch.note: So 'the same year as a little rover on the Moon' is right

pioneer_jupiter.claim: Pioneer 10 flew past Jupiter in December 1973

pioneer_last_signal.claim: Pioneer 10's last signal reached Earth on 23 January 2003
